story: Memorial Hermann Health System announced on September 8th, 2026 that its Houston clinicians are using Epic's Art assistant to draft the plain-language note a patient receives with a lab or imaging result, and published three figures for the effect. A trade publication named two days later what those figures do not establish, and Texas law in force since January 1st, 2026 requires a provider using an artificial intelligence system in relation to health care service or treatment to make a disclosure to the recipient.

claims.text: Memorial Hermann Health System says its clinicians are using an artificial intelligence tool built directly into Epic to help patients understand their test results.
claims.quote: Clinicians at Memorial Hermann Health System (MHHS) are using a new artificial intelligence (AI) tool built directly into Epic to help patients better understand their test results and to make informed decisions about next steps in their care journey.
claims.source_title: Memorial Hermann Health System Clinicians Use Epic's AI Tool to Help Patients Better Understand Test Results
claims.notes: Dateline reads HOUSTON, Sept. 8, 2026. This is the health system's own announcement, not a regulator's finding. Every figure in c5 to c7 is the announcer's own.

claims.text: Epic's Art is described by the announcement as an assistant that streamlines clinician documentation.
claims.quote: Epic's Art is an AI-powered assistant that helps clinicians streamline documentation.
claims.source_title: Memorial Hermann Health System Clinicians Use Epic's AI Tool to Help Patients Better Understand Test Results
claims.notes: The tool's name is Art, capital A only, no quotation marks in the source.

claims.text: The draft is generated in real time while the clinician reviews lab and imaging results in Epic's In Basket, and it is written in patient-friendly language rather than medical terms.
claims.quote: As clinicians review lab and imaging results in Epic's In Basket, Art helps generate an initial draft patient note in real time, using clear, patient-friendly language instead of complex medical terms.
claims.source_title: Memorial Hermann Health System Clinicians Use Epic's AI Tool to Help Patients Better Understand Test Results
claims.notes: In Basket is Epic's product name and takes two capitalised words.

claims.text: The clinician reviews, edits and personalizes the draft before it reaches the patient.
claims.quote: Clinicians can then review, edit and personalize the draft, giving them more time to focus on the patient's care and next steps.
claims.source_title: Memorial Hermann Health System Clinicians Use Epic's AI Tool to Help Patients Better Understand Test Results
claims.notes: The source says clinicians CAN review and edit. It does not say every draft is reviewed, and the deck must not upgrade can to does.

claims.text: The health system reports that patients sent 32% fewer follow-up messages about test results when clinicians started from Art's draft.
claims.quote: Since Memorial Hermann began using the feature, patients have sent 32% fewer follow-up messages about test results when clinicians started with Art's draft, reducing the number of return questions while helping patients receive the information they need at the time they receive their results.
claims.source_title: Memorial Hermann Health System Clinicians Use Epic's AI Tool to Help Patients Better Understand Test Results
claims.notes: Printed as 32% with the percent sign, no space. Fewer than what is not stated in the release. See c13, which says what this figure describes.

claims.text: Art has helped the health system's care teams write over 55,000 messages to patients, by the health system's own count.
claims.quote: Art has helped Memorial Hermann's care teams write over 55,000 messages to patients.
claims.source_title: Memorial Hermann Health System Clinicians Use Epic's AI Tool to Help Patients Better Understand Test Results
claims.notes: Printed as 55,000 with a thousands comma and the qualifier over. Never render it as 55000 or as an exact count.

claims.text: The health system puts the time saving at an average of nine seconds per result comment for clinicians who started from Art's draft.
claims.quote: So far, clinicians who have started with Art's draft have saved an average of nine seconds per result comment.
claims.source_title: Memorial Hermann Health System Clinicians Use Epic's AI Tool to Help Patients Better Understand Test Results
claims.notes: SPELLED OUT as nine seconds in this source, not 9 seconds. The healthsystemCIO article renders the same figure as 9 seconds. If the deck cites the health system, spell it.

claims.text: Memorial Hermann's chief medical information officer calls the tool a starting point that clinicians review, edit and personalize before sharing with the patient.
claims.quote: The starting point that Art provides is incredibly helpful in providing more thorough and informative test result follow-up notes that clinicians can review, edit and personalize before sharing with the patient,
claims.source_title: Memorial Hermann Health System Clinicians Use Epic's AI Tool to Help Patients Better Understand Test Results
claims.notes: Attributed on the page to Dr. Ryan Walsh, associate vice president and chief medical information officer for Memorial Hermann Health System. The quote ends with a comma inside the closing quotation mark because the attribution follows it.

claims.text: The same officer says the technology is designed to support rather than replace the clinician's judgment and relationship with the patient.
claims.quote: This technology is designed to support, not replace, the role of the clinician's judgment and relationship with the patient.
claims.source_title: Memorial Hermann Health System Clinicians Use Epic's AI Tool to Help Patients Better Understand Test Results
claims.notes: Same speaker as c8, Dr. Ryan Walsh. This is a design intention stated by the vendor's customer, not a measured outcome.

claims.text: Memorial Hermann piloted the feature in December of 2025 in its innovation clinic and has since expanded use across the system.
claims.quote: Memorial Hermann piloted the feature in December of 2025 in their innovation clinic for clinician feedback and has quickly expanded use across the System.
claims.source_title: Memorial Hermann Health System Clinicians Use Epic's AI Tool to Help Patients Better Understand Test Results
claims.notes: December of 2025 is the only date the release gives for the pilot. No end date for the pilot and no start date for system-wide use is stated, so the period the figures in c5 to c7 cover is not established.

claims.text: An Epic senior director of research and development says the deployment gives other organizations a model for rolling this out at scale.
claims.quote: This approach provides other organizations a model for rolling this out at scale
claims.source_title: Memorial Hermann Health System Clinicians Use Epic's AI Tool to Help Patients Better Understand Test Results
claims.notes: Attributed to Shashank Raghu, senior director of R and D for Clinical Communications and Mobile Solutions at Epic. The trailing comma from the attribution clause is removed so the quote is a clean substring of the page.

claims.text: A trade publication notes that all three figures come from Epic and its customer, with no baseline, control arm or denominator alongside them.
claims.quote: All three figures come from Epic and its customer. No baseline, control arm or denominator accompanies them.
claims.source_title: healthsystemCIO, In Basket AI and the wrong metric
claims.notes: By Anthony Guerra, published September 10th, 2026, two days after the announcement. The three figures are the 32%, the 55,000 and the time saving.

claims.text: The same publication says the 32% describes clinicians who chose to work from a draft.
claims.quote: Specifically, the 32% describes clinicians who chose to work from a draft.
claims.source_title: healthsystemCIO, In Basket AI and the wrong metric
claims.notes: This is the selection point and it is the article's, not the docket's. The deck may state it as the publication's characterisation and must not state it as a finding of the health system.

claims.text: The publication points to a randomized pilot of 52 doctors at UC San Diego Health in 2023. Reply time moved less than 6% and missed statistical significance, and read time climbed almost 22%.
claims.quote: Physicians at UC San Diego Health tested Epic's AI draft replies in a randomized pilot of 52 doctors in 2023. Reply time moved less than 6% and missed statistical significance, so the efficiency case failed on its own terms in the first controlled test. Read time, meanwhile, climbed almost 22%.
claims.source_title: healthsystemCIO, In Basket AI and the wrong metric
claims.notes: That pilot tested AI draft REPLIES to patient messages, which is not the same feature as the result-comment drafting at Memorial Hermann. The deck must not present it as a test of the same thing.

claims.text: Texas Business and Commerce Code Section 552.051(f) requires the provider of a health care service or treatment to give the disclosure under Subsection (b) to the recipient. The timing is no later than the date the service or treatment is first provided, with an emergency carve-out.
claims.quote: If an artificial intelligence system is used in relation to health care service or treatment, the provider of the service or treatment shall provide the disclosure under Subsection (b) to the recipient of the service or treatment or the recipient's personal representative not later than the date the service or treatment is first provided, except in the case of emergency, in which case the provider shall provide the required disclosure as soon as reasonably possible.
claims.source_title: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 552, Section 552.051, Disclosure to Consumers
claims.notes: SCOPE IS AMBIGUOUS AND THE DECK MUST WRITE TO THE AMBIGUITY. The word governmental does not appear in (f). The competing reading is that (f) only sets timing for a duty that arises under (b), whose duty-holder is a governmental agency. Chapter 552 has no applicability section that resolves it. Do NOT write that this provision requires Memorial Hermann to disclose.
claims.document: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 552, Artificial Intelligence Protection

claims.text: Subsection (b) of the same section places its disclosure duty on a governmental agency that makes an artificial intelligence system available to interact with consumers.
claims.quote: A governmental agency that makes available an artificial intelligence system intended to interact with consumers shall disclose to each consumer, before or at the time of interaction, that the consumer is interacting with an artificial intelligence system.
claims.source_title: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 552, Section 552.051, Disclosure to Consumers
claims.notes: This is the subsection (f) points back to. It must be shown beside c15 rather than instead of it.
claims.document: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 552, Artificial Intelligence Protection

claims.text: A disclosure under that subsection must be clear and conspicuous, must be written in plain language, and may not use a dark pattern as defined by Section 541.001.
claims.quote: must be clear and conspicuous
claims.source_title: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 552, Section 552.051(d), Disclosure to Consumers
claims.notes: The fact-checker held the full three part list at medium confidence on WHITESPACE only, because the statute page sets (1), (2) and (3) on their own lines and the conversion flattened them. The quote is narrowed to the one clause whose rendering is certain.
claims.document: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 552, Artificial Intelligence Protection

claims.text: Section 552.102 directs the attorney general to maintain an online mechanism on the attorney general's website through which a consumer may submit a complaint under the chapter.
claims.quote: The attorney general shall create and maintain an online mechanism on the attorney general's Internet website through which a consumer may submit a complaint under this chapter to the attorney general.
claims.source_title: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 552, Sec. 552.102, Information and Complaints
claims.notes: The statute does not give a URL for the mechanism and this run did not confirm the mechanism exists in fact, only that the statute requires one.
claims.document: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 552, Artificial Intelligence Protection

claims.text: The attorney general holds exclusive authority to enforce the chapter, except to the extent provided by Section 552.106.
claims.quote: The attorney general has exclusive authority to enforce this chapter, except to the extent provided by Section 552.106.
claims.source_title: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 552, Sec. 552.101, Enforcement Authority
claims.notes: Sec. 552.101(a). Section 552.106 is headed ENFORCEMENT ACTIONS BY STATE AGENCIES and its text was not fetched, so the deck may not characterise what the exception covers.
claims.document: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 552, Artificial Intelligence Protection

claims.text: The chapter gives no private right of action for a violation of it or of any other law.
claims.quote: This chapter does not provide a basis for, and is not subject to, a private right of action for a violation of this chapter or any other law.
claims.source_title: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 552, Sec. 552.101, Enforcement Authority
claims.notes: Sec. 552.101(b). A patient has no suit of their own under this chapter, which is the point that pairs with c18.
claims.document: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 552, Artificial Intelligence Protection

claims.text: The section defines health care services as services related to human health, or to the diagnosis, prevention or treatment of a human disease or impairment. The provider must be an individual licensed, registered or certified to provide them.
claims.quote: means services related to human health or to the diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of a human disease or impairment provided by an individual licensed, registered, or certified under applicable state or federal law to provide those services
claims.source_title: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 552, Section 552.051(a), Disclosure to Consumers
claims.notes: The quote is narrowed past the defined term so the quotation-mark delimiter the fetch could not confirm falls outside it. The definition attaches to an INDIVIDUAL licensed, registered or certified, while (f)'s duty falls on the provider of the service or treatment, and the section does not define provider.
claims.document: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 552, Artificial Intelligence Protection

claims.text: Subsection (c) states that a person must make the disclosure regardless of whether it would be obvious to a reasonable consumer that they are interacting with an artificial intelligence system.
claims.quote: A person is required to make the disclosure under Subsection (b) regardless of whether it would be obvious to a reasonable consumer that the consumer is interacting with an artificial intelligence system.
claims.source_title: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 552, Section 552.051(c), Disclosure to Consumers
claims.notes: The strongest textual evidence that Sec. 552.051 is not confined to governmental agencies, because (c) says a person where (b) says a governmental agency. It is evidence about the ambiguity in c15, not a resolution of it.
claims.document: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 552, Artificial Intelligence Protection

claims.text: Section 552.051 was added by House Bill 149 of the 89th Legislature and took effect on January 1st, 2026.
claims.quote: eff. January 1, 2026.
claims.source_title: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 552, Section 552.051, enactment note
claims.notes: The full enactment note reads Added by Acts 2025, 89th Leg., R.S., Ch. 1174 (H.B. 149), Sec. 4, eff. January 1, 2026. The acts year is 2025 and the effective date is 2026, so the deck must not collapse them into one year.

rejected.finding: That Texas law requires Memorial Hermann Health System to disclose its use of Art to patients.
rejected.reason: Not established by the text. Sec. 552.051(b) puts its duty on a governmental agency, and (f) extends the disclosure under Subsection (b) to the provider of the service or treatment without saying whether that provider must be governmental. Chapter 552 has no applicability section resolving it, no court construction was fetched, and no attorney general guidance was fetched. Verified as an ambiguity in c15, c16 and c22 instead. The deck must present the question, not the answer.

rejected.finding: That Memorial Hermann is in violation of, or non-compliant with, Chapter 552.
rejected.reason: Nothing fetched this run supports it. No enforcement action, no complaint and no agency finding was located, and the underlying scope question in c15 is unresolved.

rejected.finding: A healthsystemCIO sentence about the clinician's review keeping the message in the clinician's voice and under their name.
rejected.reason: The fetch returned only a fragment without its opening clause or sentence boundary, so it cannot be quoted character for character. The idea is covered by c4 from the primary source.

rejected.finding: That the article's time-saving figure is 9 seconds, rendered with the numeral.
rejected.reason: The numeral was returned in a fetcher's summary list, not inside a verbatim sentence. The verified rendering of that figure is nine seconds, spelled out, in the press release at c7.

rejected.finding: A dateline time of 10:00 ET on the press release.
rejected.reason: Two fetches of the same page disagreed on whether the time appears. Only the date is common to both, so only the date is carried, in c1.

rejected.finding: Any characterisation of what Sec. 552.106 permits state agencies to do.
rejected.reason: Its text was not fetched. Only its heading and the cross-reference in c19 are established.

rejected.finding: An About Memorial Hermann Health System boilerplate paragraph and its contents.
rejected.reason: The second fetch reports no such paragraph on the page, with the release ending at media contact information.

rejected.finding: The full three part rendering of Sec. 552.051(d) as one verbatim quote.
rejected.reason: Held at medium confidence on whitespace by the fact-checker, because the statute page sets the subdivisions on their own lines and the conversion flattened them. c17 carries only the clause whose rendering is certain.

absences.claim: The Memorial Hermann announcement never says that patients are told, notified or otherwise informed that the note they receive began as an AI-generated draft.
absences.document_searched: Memorial Hermann Health System press release, HOUSTON, Sept. 8, 2026, distributed by PR Newswire, read in full
absences.how_established: The full body was retrieved and read on two separate fetches of the page, six paragraphs from the Houston dateline through the Epic quote. A targeted second pass searched the entire page including the SOURCE line and media contact block for the strings disclose, disclosure, notify, notified, inform patients, told, transparen and label, and none of them appears anywhere on the page. The release describes the clinician reviewing and editing the draft before sharing it with the patient, and says nothing about what the patient is told regarding the draft's origin.

absences.claim: The healthsystemCIO article does not address whether patients are told a message was AI-drafted.
absences.document_searched: healthsystemCIO, In Basket AI and the wrong metric, by Anthony Guerra, Sept. 10, 2026
absences.how_established: A targeted pass asked for any sentence in the article mentioning whether patients are told the message was AI-drafted. No such sentence appears. The article's critique is about what the three figures do not establish, not about patient disclosure.

absences.claim: Neither the announcement nor the article mentions Texas Business and Commerce Code Chapter 552, House Bill 149, TRAIGA, or any Texas disclosure obligation.
absences.document_searched: Memorial Hermann Health System press release of Sept. 8, 2026
absences.how_established: The full text of the release was read and contains no reference to any statute, regulation or legal obligation, and the term search for disclose and disclosure returned nothing on the page. The link between the deployment and Chapter 552 is the docket's own juxtaposition of two separately verified documents and is presented as such, never as a connection either document draws.

absences.claim: Chapter 552 contains no section headed APPLICABILITY or SCOPE that resolves whether Sec. 552.051(f) reaches a private health care provider.
absences.document_searched: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 552, full section list as printed on the Texas statutes page
absences.how_established: The chapter's complete section list was transcribed from the page. Subchapter A holds Sec. 552.001 DEFINITIONS, Sec. 552.002 CONSTRUCTION OF CHAPTER and Sec. 552.003 LOCAL PREEMPTION. Subchapter B holds Sec. 552.051 through Sec. 552.057 and Subchapter C holds Sec. 552.101 through Sec. 552.106. No section in the list is headed APPLICABILITY or SCOPE. The texts of Sec. 552.001 and Sec. 552.002 were not fetched this run, so this establishes only that no section is so headed.

absences.claim: Sec. 552.051(f) does not contain the word governmental.
absences.document_searched: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Sec. 552.051, Disclosure to Consumers, subsection (f)
absences.how_established: Subsection (f) was transcribed verbatim on three separate fetches and a direct term check confirmed the word governmental does not appear in it. The duty-holder named in (f) is the provider of the service or treatment, with no qualifier.
